mapping: image u in [0,1] left to right over 360 deg, v in [0,1] top to bottom over the full source sphere; azimuth a=(u-0.5)*2*pi, elevation e=(0.5-v)*pi; direction=[sin(a)cos(e), sin(e), -cos(a)cos(e)], so u=0.5 looks down -z, u=0.75 looks down +x, +y up. The webp holds only elevations +90 to -25 (its rows cover v from 0 to 0.6389 of the source).
encoding: v = clamp((L*k)^(1/2.2), 0, 1), L linear radiance, 8-bit RGB
percentile: 99.5th percentile of Rec.709 luminance over the cropped pixels, sun disc (5 deg) excluded, unweighted; maps to 0.96
sunDirectionThreeEquirectUvNote: same sun expressed for three.js equirectUv (u=atan(z,x)/2pi+0.5, which puts u=0.5 at +x); use this one if the image is fed to three.js as an equirect texture unchanged
